notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation for Dedicated capacity focused on throughput guarantees and SLA language. Velox is an adtech vendor running real-time bidding + personalization reranks during campaign windows. Extremely latency sensitive during peak auctions; cost-conscious but will pay for guaranteed throughput for campaign reliability.

Recent timeline / activity (bulleted):
- 2026-01-20: initial inbound, qualified by AE (Avery). basic requirements call.
- 2026-02-05: deep-dive with SE (Diego) — load profile shared (see drive).
- 2026-02-18: POC kickoff, stress test run (fireflies ff_2026-02-18_velox_poc).
- 2026-02-25: POC interim sync — engineering saw CPU/KV cache issues with default batcher.
- 2026-03-03: SLA negotiation call (legal + infra) — recorded ff_2026-03-03_sla-negotiation.
- 2026-03-08: pricing follow-up, procurement signals; requested SOW language examples.

POC results (engineer notes, shorthand):
- Model: openchat-7b-quant (customer preference) + redwood-v5 fallback for cost spikes.
- Observed sustained throughput: ~140k tokens/sec across 6 pre-warmed GPUs (p50 latency ~35ms).
- Observed burst: up to 230k tokens/sec for short windows (10–12 min) when KV cache hits high.
- Latency: p95 ~300–350ms at peak concurrency, p99 spikes to ~650ms under coldpath requests.
- Concurrency pattern: steady baseline 120 concurrent streams, peak concurrency 420 during campaign ramps.

Customer asks / negotiation points (direct quotes + paraphrase):
- "We cannot dip below 180k tokens/sec during campaign windows — it's a hard SLA for auctions." (VP Eng)
- Wants explicit concurrency caps and guaranteed min tokens/sec; also wants burst allowance for launch days.
- Insists on data residency + KMS control for bidder logs.

Redwood proposal (draft positions discussed on 2026-03-03):
- Base guaranteed throughput: 120k tokens/sec (sustained) for committed tier (reserved 6x A100-eq nodes).
- Customer counter: requests guaranteed 180k sustained.
- Concurrency caps: base concurrency cap 300 streams; can request temporary increase to 500 with 12-hour notice (or auto-burst when pre-funded).
- Burst policy: allow +50% burst (relative to guaranteed) for up to 10 minutes/hour without additional charge; extended bursts billed at premium.
- Pre-warmed nodes: recommend reserved 8 nodes (dedicated) + 2 hot spares to meet customer's 180k target with headroom.
- Autoscale rules: scale-up to burst pool within 30s using pre-pulled quantized kernels; scale-down 5–10 minutes.

SLA / penalties discussion items:
- Define tokens/sec as measured at ingress after routing and queuing — need common measurement point.
- Credits tied to % below guaranteed min tokens/sec during business-critical windows (campaign windows only).
- Latency SLOs: propose p95 <= 250ms on baseline small payloads; customer wants p95 <=200ms for auction-critical flows.
- Observability: 90-day retention for per-route metrics; customer requested 365-day audit logs for compliance.

Cost / reserved planning:
- Redwood pricing sketch provided in drive link. Customer trying to balance capex (reserved nodes) vs variable (burst).
- Estimated ARR ramp: $500k–1M depending on final guaranteed throughput and burst inclusion.
- Technical tradeoff: more reserved GPUs reduces variable price and simplifies SLA but increases upfront commit.

Open technical risks / blockers:
- Measurement disagreement risk: need a shared telemetry hook (trace id mapping) to resolve disputes.
- Model variance: openchat-7b quant gets better throughput but quality/regression tests required; fallback to redwood-v5 must be transparent to app.
- Cold-start p99 spikes for rare large-context requests — potentially mitigated by prefix caching and keep-alive sessions.

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood to produce two SOW options by 2026-03-12: (A) 120k guaranteed baseline + standard burst; (B) 180k guaranteed with additional reserved nodes and higher ARR. (owner: Avery + Diego)
- Legal to provide SLA credit language draft; customer to send procurement template (gmail thread th_3f8c1_sla-draft).
- Technical: schedule stress test v2 (sim target 180k sustained, 24-hour run) week of 2026-03-15. (ticket INF-4321)
- Next stakeholder sync: 2026-03-17 11:00 PT — include VP Eng, Infra lead, Diego, Avery, Priya.

CRM notes / shorthand:
- Customer tone: pragmatic but firm on guaranteed throughput. "We run live auctions; downtime or degraded throughput = revenue loss."
- Procurement: finance wants ARR cap clarified before exec sign-off.
- Suggest moving conversation to procurement stage after SOW options and 24h stress test.

Linked artifacts: pricing deck (drive), SLA draft (drive), POC logs (attached to INF-4321), security questionnaire in SEC-2109.

Short checklist for AE/SE:
- [ ] Finalize measurement point & telemetry spec (trace id mapping).
- [ ] Prepare SOW A/B with explicit token/sec math and node counts.
- [ ] Confirm burst billing cadence and pre-funded burst bucket option.
